title: An idle fleet costs the database one watermark read per pass: the loop's steps run when the event log moves or a timer is due, on indexed, prepared statements, every decision and timer unchanged
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/loops.rs, `resident_loop` (one pass: `bridge.tick()`, `observer.tick()`, the disk watch, `dispatch::step`, `supervise::keep_residents`, `supervise::keep_alive`, then `pause_unless_stopped`) and `loop_interval()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/config.rs; in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs `step()`, `load()` and `load_stalls()`; in crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs `Work::load` and `attempts()` (the due times of a retry: `NOT_READY_RETRY_MS` after a refusal, `retry_wait_ms()` after a failure); dispatch/stall.rs (`Bounds`, a stall's age measured from its record) and dispatch/stops.rs (a failed Stop's retry); `keep_residents`, `keep_alive` and `revive` in crates/spawn-cli/src/supervise.rs (the revive backoff); `CHECK_EVERY` in crates/spawn-cli/src/disk.rs; `Bridge::tick` and `catch_up` in crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs (the claim loop, `lease_ttl`); in crates/spawn-postgres: `DISPATCH_FACTS` in src/fleet.rs (six correlated reads of spawn_commands per session), `STALL_FACTS`, `delivery_rows`, `mission_news`, `residents_to_keep` and `liveness_facts`, `query_json`/`query_one` in src/lib.rs (every statement parsed and planned afresh), and in sql/schema.sql the `spawn_commands` table and its indexes (only `spawn_commands_open`, partial), `spawn_submit` (which appends `command.accepted`), `spawn_claim`, `spawn_finish` and `spawn_append_trusted` (which already runs `pg_notify('spawn_events', id)` on every append; nothing LISTENs); docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 and docs/design.md §14.

The problem. Measured on the live database on 2026-11-06: pg_stat_user_tables counts 17.8 million sequential scans of spawn_commands (287 rows), 1.2 million of mission_residents and about 0.75 million each of mission_tasks, mission_missions and spawn_session_state, about 130 table scans per loop pass at two passes a second, around the clock. Every pass of `spawn loop` runs the dispatcher's whole step (the dispatch facts, the mission rows, the stall facts, the gate room records), the residents' and the supervisor's liveness, the Bridge's catch-up and claim and the Observer's read, though in an idle fleet nothing has changed since the pass before; the dispatch facts read spawn_commands six times per session through correlated subqueries no index serves, and every statement is parsed and planned again. The owner's goal (2026-11-06) is the Pareto frontier: no dimension improves by letting another regress. This cost must go with no decision moved and no timer late.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. Run on change. The loop keeps the event watermark (max spawn_events.id) each of its steps last acted on. A pass runs the dispatcher's step (`dispatch::step`, with `Work::load`), `keep_residents`, `keep_alive`, the Bridge's catch-up and command claim, and the Observer's read of new events only when the watermark has moved since that step last ran, or when one of its timers is due (2). A pass where neither holds reads the watermark once (one cheap statement: an index-only read of spawn_events' primary key, or the notifications drained, 3) and nothing else from the database. The Bridge goes on reading screens and transcripts on its own schedule (objective 025 changes that, not this one).
2. Timers, at the same times. Every action that happens today because time passed happens at the same time: a delivery retry at its `due_ms` (`attempts()`), a stall when its bound is reached (dispatch/stall.rs), a failed Stop's retry (dispatch/stops.rs), a revive after its backoff (supervise.rs), the claim of a command whose lease expired (`lease_until_ms`), the disk watch every `CHECK_EVERY`, and any other deadline a step waits for. Each step returns the earliest time it waits for; the loop runs that step then, whether or not anything else happened. A due time a step cannot compute is due now: never later than today.
3. Wake on a notification. Between passes the loop waits on `LISTEN spawn_events` (on a connection of its own), with a timeout of the earlier of the pass interval (`SPAWN_LOOP_INTERVAL_MS`, which the Bridge's screens still need) and the next due time; a notification ends the wait at once, so a change is acted on sooner than today, never later. Notifications in a burst are drained and acted on in one pass. A lost notification costs at most one interval: the watermark read is the record, a notification only a hint.
4. The same decisions. Nothing a step decides depends on how often it ran: given the same records and the same clock it makes the same orders, deliveries, escalations and digests as today, under the same keys and tags.
5. Indexes. `spawn init-db` creates two plain (not partial) btree indexes on spawn_commands, keyed exactly (session_id, id) and (session_id, principal, id) (an existing database gets them too, `create index if not exists`), and the dispatch facts' per-session reads use them: on a table of 20,000 command rows their plan holds no sequential scan of spawn_commands.
6. Prepared once. The fixed statements the loop runs (the watermark read, the dispatch facts, the stall facts, the mission rows, the liveness facts, the claim) are prepared once per connection (`prepare_cached`) and reused.
7. Causality (§14): a step acts on a record (the watermark names everything up to it) or on a due time computed from records (an attempt's `finished_at_ms`, a stall's record, a lease's `lease_until_ms`); a notification, or none, proves nothing, and time alone decides only when to look again.

How the saving shows, in numbers. The scenario's fleet (a supervisor and three residents) costs today, on an idle minute, 14,221-14,256 table scans (about 118 a pass: spawn_events 8,740, spawn_commands 4,164, mission_tasks 520, mission_residents 312, mission_missions 312, spawn_session_state 208) and 3,400 transactions; the scenario allows 150. On the live fleet it is some 22 million table scans a day that go when nothing happens, and a busy minute pays a full pass only in the half-seconds where something happened (68 of 120 in the scenario's busy minute). 017's scorecard has no dimension for database load (throughput, lead time, first-pass quality, rework, autonomy, reliability, cost in model tokens and gate time); on it the change must show nothing at all: lead time no longer and reliability (spent deliveries, stalls) no worse. The scenario holds the timers to today's measured times.

State the rule in the module comments of loops.rs and dispatch.rs, in docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 (the dispatcher's pass) and in docs/design.md §14 (a notification is a hint; the watermark is the record). Add unit tests: the next due time of each timer (a refused delivery, a failed one, a stall of each step, a Stop's retry, a revive backoff, a lease); a pass with the watermark unmoved and nothing due runs no step; one with the watermark moved runs each step once; a due time reached runs its step with the watermark unmoved; a step decides the same orders from the same facts whether it ran on every pass or only on change. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: init-db makes both indexes on a fresh and on an existing schema, and the dispatch facts over 20,000 command rows plan no sequential scan of spawn_commands.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/023.sh (read it: its header lists today's measures). A real `spawn loop` (no model judge) runs a supervisor and three residents, `alpha`, `frail` and `idle`, on a fake engine at the default pass interval (500 ms); the measure is the sum of seq_scan and idx_scan over every user table of the scenario's own database (pg_stat_statements is not installed), with transactions committed beside it. It checks:
- (1) after init-db, spawn_commands has plain indexes keyed exactly (session_id, id) and (session_id, principal, id);
- (2) an idle minute (every session waiting, no task, no command pending, nothing due) costs at most 150 table scans;
- (3) a busy minute, in which T1 is assigned to alpha (whose engine then stays busy and quiet), T2 to frail (whose text the tmux wrapper refuses to stage until 32 s in) and the supervisor is pinged four times: T1 is delivered within 4 s of its assignment; every retry of T2's delivery is made 5.0-6.5 s after the attempt before it finished (NOT_READY_RETRY_MS is 5 s), and the first after the fix goes through; each of T1's activity stalls (SPAWN_STALL_ACTIVITY_SECS=20) reaches the supervisor once, no sooner than its due time and no later than 2.5 s after it; and the minute costs at most 150 table scans plus 150 for each half-second slice that held an event.
On the live main (49b92be; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1): "(1) spawn_commands has no plain index on (session_id,id) after `spawn init-db` (its plain indexes' keys: id principal,idempotency_key; the per-session reads of the dispatch facts scan the table)". With BB_023_MEASURE=1 (only to show today's behaviour) it goes on and fails at (2), "an idle minute (no task open, no command pending, 0 events appended, nothing due) cost 14256 table scans (10719 sequential, 3537 by index; ...)", and at (3)'s scan bound (14,753 scans against 150 + 150 x 68 = 10,350); its timing checks pass today (T1 delivered in 1.8-1.9 s, retries 5.34-5.51 s, stall digests 0.1-0.5 s after due), which is what the change must keep. It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
